params.body:
**Triage proposal** (from the forwarded mail; change the labels if it is wrong)
Category: request  Priority: P2
Summary: A deck on young people and self-employment, made with Gentells, leaned on Belgian and European series that Gentells does not hold. They should be in Gentells so the next run can cite them from there.

Source: Portal mail:51.

## What is asked

Hold these series structurally, as the backbone for work on young people and self-employment in Belgium:

- RSVZ, yearly figures on the self-employed (May)
- StarterAtlas (July)
- VDAB, list of shortage occupations (February)
- Securex barometers (several a year)
- TUI Stiftung, Young Europe youth study (June/July)
- Eurostat, self-employed by age, quarterly

## Where this stands (checked 2026-11-15)

| Series | In Gentells |
|---|---|
| RSVZ | not held |
| StarterAtlas | not held |
| VDAB shortage occupations | only VDAB Trends (`source-gt-569`), proposed, never read |
| Securex | news page (`source-gt-578`), proposed, never read; the press room has a live feed (`press.securex.be/feed`) that is not listed |
| TUI Stiftung Young Europe | not held |
| Eurostat self-employed by age | not held; the dataset is `lfsq_esgaed` and answers without a key |

## What a pull request can do, and what it cannot

A third source list (`research/source-list-2026-11-15.json`) adds the missing rows as proposals, the same way as the lists of 20 October and 9 November. After `bin/import-source-list.mjs --apply` on the box they exist in Gentells, and the Securex press feed can go on trial.

That alone does not put them in a deck. Reference rows are never fetched and never become signals: a figure from them reaches a reader only as a statistic cited under a sentence of a live post (`bin/cite-statistics.mjs`). The reading side is #424 (the reference layer, Eurostat as the pilot); the figures themselves are the separate issue on the deck's key figures.
params.title: Hold the Belgian and European series on young people and self-employment (RSVZ, StarterAtlas, VDAB, Securex, TUI, Eurostat)
